presentation.label: USB AUDIO
presentation.summary: Record stereo mixes or individual tracks over USB, or send them to Outbox 8 at 44.1 kHz and 24 bits.
presentation.overview: Choose one USB output layout in Modwerk: Main, Main + Cue, Track 8 / Master, eight tracks before LEVEL, eight tracks following LEVEL, or eight tracks plus Main and Cue. The updated shared USB stack supports the Outbox 8 44.1 kHz handshake. Modwerk stores a routing plan; apply its USB channel pairs separately in Elektron’s Outbox app. Existing configurations without USB settings keep the classic twenty-channel implementation.
highlights: Six selectable stereo output layouts; 2 to 20 USB channels
Outbox 8 rate handshake and shared audio / MIDI reset handling
Saved four-pair Outbox routing plan and per-layout CPU estimates
usage: Open USB Audio setup, choose Computer or Outbox 8, and select the audio to send. Read the signal-tap description and save the setup before adding it.
For Outbox 8, assign up to four stereo sources to the physical outputs. Match the shown USB pairs in Elektron’s Outbox app; Modwerk does not program the Outbox.
For Computer, select the Octatrack USB input in your recording software and use the shown stereo channel pairs. Full multichannel operation requires high-speed USB.

To return to the classic twenty-channel source, choose Computer and Use classic 20-channel setup. This removes the new settings; existing saved configurations without USB settings keep their prior code path.

limitations: Output only, fixed 44.1 kHz / 24-bit; USB input and Crossbar variants are excluded.
One audio layout per build; shared USB MIDI is included.
Like every DRAM module, gives up about 10 MB of sample memory: projects that filled Flex/recorder memory can show OUT OF MEMORY. Shorten recorder reservations or load long samples into Static (#433).
Outbox assignments are a plan and must be applied in Elektron’s Outbox app.
At full speed, track feeds fall back to a stereo sum and Main + Cue to Main.
Post-LEVEL tracks exclude MAIN LEVEL and master effects on tracks 1–7. With a master track, tracks 1–7 lead track 8 by 32 samples.
Current-build Octatrack / Outbox operation, chip timing, complete memory bounds, Windows and Linux host behavior are not tested.

storage.label: Audio rings
storage.conditions: Exact linked section sizes are recorded per layout in evidence/layouts.json; the historical 88 KiB figure applies to the classic twenty-channel path. Complete stack / DMA and hardware memory bounds have not been measured.

processing.label: CPU load
processing.conditions: Upstream records sustained hardware captures and MIDI traffic, not a comparable hardware CPU utilization percentage.

impact.conditions: Audio modules are rated for an active instance, including expensive modes and changing controls; MIDI/USB features are rated while enabled. More tracks or instances increase demand. Shared runtime reservations and reused stock buffers are not added again per module. These rough source-backed tiers do not establish hardware headroom or qualification.

cpu.rationale: Relative per-layout source estimates: Main, Main/Cue and Track 8 are low, eight pre-LEVEL tracks moderate, twenty-channel and post-LEVEL tracks high. Pinned upstream port instruction counts are not chip cycle or utilization measurements.

dsp.rationale: The documented stream taps the existing DSP/CPU exchange and MAIN/CUE output words. It does not add a new DSP audio algorithm. Minimal is an estimate of additional DSP work, not zero bus or system contention.

memory.rationale: The selected source determines the static audio ring footprint. Linked sections are recorded for all six layouts in evidence/layouts.json. This tier describes source allocation sizes, not a complete hardware memory bound.

tests.summary: Software checks cover six source-only layouts, GNU runtime linking, guarded hooks, packaging and configuration persistence. Owner approved this experimental release without physical hardware testing. Hardware operation, real-chip timing and complete memory bounds remain unmeasured.

tutorial.title: Record a mix or send Main + Cue to Outbox
steps: Choose and save: open USB Audio setup, choose Outbox 8 and Main + Cue mixes, then Assign in order. Save the setup to the named configuration and build locally from your own OS 1.40C file.

Connect and route: connect the Octatrack USB port to Outbox 8. In Elektron's Outbox app, match Main / USB 1/2 to physical outputs 1/2 and Cue / USB 3/4 to physical outputs 3/4. Modwerk stores this plan; it does not program the Outbox hardware.

Use and reset: Main is the final stereo mix; Cue is the separate stereo Cue bus. Outputs 5/6 and 7/8 are off. To use different signals, change and save the source and assignments, rebuild, and update the external app. Stop the stream before changing cabling.
